<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|174|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XII.}}</noinclude>al numbered. Feare not therfore: you are more vvorth then many sparowes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=8}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10, 32. Mar. 8, 38.''}}* And I say to you, {{sup|‖}} Euery one that confesseth me before men, the Sonne of man also vvil confesse him before the Angels of God. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=9}}† But he that denieth me before men, shal be denied before the Angels of God. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=10}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 33. Mr. 3, 28.''}}* And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''See Annot. Mt. 12, 32.''}}* euery one that speaketh a vvord against the sonne of man, it shal be forgiuen him: but he that shal blaspheme against the holy Ghost, to him it shal not be forgiuen. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10, 19. Mar. 13, 11.''}}* And vvhen they shal bring you in to the synagogs and to magistrates and potestates, {{sup|‖}} be not careful in what maner, and vvhat you shal ansvver, or vvhat you shal say. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=12}}† For the holy Ghost shal teach you in the very houre vvhat you must say.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=13}}† And one of the multitude said to him, Maister, speake to my brother that he deuide the inheritaunce vvith me. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=14}}† But he said to him, Man, {{sup|‖}} vvho hath appointed me iudge or deuider ouer you? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=15}}† And he said to them, See and bevvare of al auarice: for not in any mans aboundance doth his life consist, of those things vvhich he possesseth. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=16}}† And he spake a similitude to them, saying, A certaine riche mans field yelded plentie of fruites. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=17}}† and he thought vvithin him self, saying, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Giue it to the poore, that shouldst thou do, saith S. Basil.}}∷ VVhat shal I doe, because I haue not vvhither to gather my fruites? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=18}}† And he said, This vvil I doe, I vvil destroy my barnes, and vvil make greater: and thither vvil I gather al things that are grovven to me, and my goods, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=19}}† and I vvil say to my soule, Soule, thou hast much goods laid vp for many yeres, take thy rest, eate, drinke, make good cheere. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=20}}† But God said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ A goodly warning for al riche men.}}∷ Thou foole, this night they require thy soule of thee: and the things that thou hast prouided, vvhose shal they be? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=21}}† So is he that laieth vp treasure to him self, and is not {{sup|‖}} riche to God vvard.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=22}}† And he said to his Disciples, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 6, 25.''}}* Therfore I say to you, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He forbiddeth not competent prouidence, but to much carefulnes. See Annot. vpon S. Matth. ''c. 6, 25''.}}∷ Be not careful for your life, vvhat you shal eate: nor for your body, vvhat you shal doe on. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=23}}† The life is more then the meate, and the body is more then the raiment. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=24}}† Consider the rauens, for they sovv not, neither doe they reape, vvhich neither haue storehouse nor barne, and God feedeth them. Hovv much more are you of greater price then they? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=25}}† And vvhich of you by caring can adde to his stature one cubite? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=26}}† If then you be not able to doe so much as the least thing, for the rest vvhy are you careful? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=27}}† Consider the lilies how<noinclude>{{rh|||they}}</noinclude>
